title: Cream Cheese Semifreddo with Maple and Balsamic
changes_from_base: Yolks whisked to 71 °C and beaten with cream cheese replace the whole-egg base; maple syrup, balsamic and flaky salt replace the jam swirl.
summary: A velvety frozen dessert combining tangy cream cheese with a rich egg yolk base, finished with a sophisticated balance of sweet maple and sharp balsamic vinegar.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Line a 20 cm loaf tin with cling film. Whip 240 ml chilled double cream to stiff peaks and keep it in the fridge.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk 5 egg yolks, 100 g caster sugar, 1 tsp vanilla and ¼ tsp fine salt in a heatproof bowl. Ensure you mix them immediately so the sugar does not make the yolks grainy.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Set the bowl over gently simmering water and whisk constantly for 5-7 min until pale and 71 °C. Remove from the heat and whisk for 8-10 min until the mixture cools to room temperature.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Beat the cooled yolk mixture with 200 g softened cream cheese for 3-4 min using a stand mixer. Scrape the sides down to ensure the base is completely smooth.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Gently fold the cream cheese mixture into the whipped cream using a silicone spatula. Stop just before the two mixtures are fully incorporated to maintain the light texture.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pour the mixture into the prepared tin and wrap it well. Freeze for at least 12 h until the semifreddo is solid.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Dip the base of the tin in warm water for a few seconds, turn the semifreddo out and peel off the film. Cut 2.5 cm slices with a hot, dry knife and top each with maple syrup, a few drops of balsamic vinegar and a pinch of flaky sea salt.

tips: Warm, soft cream cheese beats in smoothly; cold cream cheese leaves small lumps.
A spoonful of sour cherries in syrup works in place of the balsamic vinegar.
safety: Use an instant-read thermometer to ensure the yolks reach the correct temperature for safety and thickness.
storage: Wrap well and keep in the freezer up to 2 weeks; slice straight from the freezer with a hot, dry knife.
